mdbisync-initial-sync.yml:
# Copy to .github/workflows/mdbisync-initial-sync.yml in a synchronized
# repository, next to the sync workflow (mdbisync.yml).
#
# Initial sync makes one side equal to the other before the first sync, and
# restores the sync after its state is lost. Run it by hand from the Actions
# tab. Without `confirm` it is a dry run: the job summary lists by path what
# it would create, overwrite, move to Linear's trash and leave out, and
# nothing is written.
#
# It is destructive to the target side:
# - git-to-linear: Linear documents of the synchronized teams and projects
#   that have no file are moved to Linear's trash (restorable there).
# - linear-to-git: one pull request removes the synchronized files that have
#   no document; a person reviews and merges it.
#
# Needs: repository variables MDBISYNC_APP_CLIENT_ID and MDBISYNC_LINEAR_CLIENT_ID.
# In the mdbisync environment limited to the tracked branch, set
# MDBISYNC_APP_PRIVATE_KEY and MDBISYNC_LINEAR_CLIENT_SECRET.
name: mdbisync initial sync

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      direction:
        description: "git-to-linear (Linear is made equal to main) or linear-to-git (a pull request makes main equal to Linear)"
        type: string
        required: true
      confirm:
        description: "Write. Leave unchecked for a dry run that writes nothing."
        type: boolean
        default: false

permissions: {}

# The same group as the sync workflow: one run at a time, never cancelled.
# GitHub keeps one pending run per group, and a newer one replaces it: if a
# sync is running when you start this workflow, a sync queued after it can
# replace this run. Disable the sync workflow while you run initial sync.
concurrency:
  group: mdbisync
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  initial-sync:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: mdbisync
    # The App token lives one hour. A longer initial sync stops here; start
    # the workflow again with the same inputs and it goes on where it stopped.
    timeout-minutes: 55
    steps:
      # Only main, the tracked branch: its files are the ones reviewed and
      # merged. A dispatch on another branch would run that branch's files in
      # a job that holds the App token and the Linear secrets. If the sync
      # tracks another branch (`tracked-branch`), name that branch here. This
      # step is in the copy of the workflow on the branch a run uses, so it
      # does not stop someone who removes it on their own branch; to keep the
      # secrets from such runs, make them secrets of an environment that only
      # main may deploy to.
      - name: Refuse a branch other than main
        shell: bash
        env:
          BRANCH: main
        # Compared in the shell: Git refs are case-sensitive, workflow expressions are not.
        run: |
          if [ "$GITHUB_REF" != "refs/heads/$BRANCH" ]; then
            echo "::error::Run this workflow on $BRANCH, not on $GITHUB_REF."
            exit 1
          fi
      - name: Check sync variables
        shell: bash
        env:
          MDBISYNC_APP_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.MDBISYNC_APP_CLIENT_ID }}
          MDBISYNC_LINEAR_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.MDBISYNC_LINEAR_CLIENT_ID }}
        run: |
          for name in MDBISYNC_APP_CLIENT_ID MDBISYNC_LINEAR_CLIENT_ID; do
            if [[ ! ${!name} =~ [^[:space:]] ]]; then
              printf '::error::Set the %s GitHub Actions variable.\n' "$name"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
      - name: Get the GitHub App token
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3.3.0
        with:
          client-id: ${{ vars.MDBISYNC_APP_CLIENT_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.MDBISYNC_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      # From Linear, the repository's hooks marked `alias: security` check
      # Linear's documents before anything is pushed; they run with pre-commit.
      - name: Install pre-commit
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # Python runs in isolated mode (-I) from the runner's temporary
          # directory, so no module of the checkout can stand in for venv or pip.
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP"

# to the initial sync workflow (mdbisync-initial-sync.yml).

# Keep this workflow disabled until the initial sync has finished: until
# then each run writes nothing and fails with `initial-sync-required`, and
# a sync queued in the shared group can replace a pending initial sync.
# Disable it again before any later initial sync (recovery), and stop your
# own dispatch timer then too.

# Each run takes Linear's changes to main through the sync pull request,
# which the sync merges once its checks pass, and writes main's changes to
# Linear. It runs on every push to main and by hand.

# from your own scheduler through workflow_dispatch:

# MDBISYNC_APP_PRIVATE_KEY and MDBISYNC_LINEAR_CLIENT_SECRET.

  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions: {}

# The same group as the initial sync: one run at a time, never cancelled.
concurrency:
  group: mdbisync
  cancel-in-progress: false

  sync:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: mdbisync

    timeout-minutes: 55

      # a job that holds the App token and the Linear secrets. If the sync

# Copy to .github/workflows/pre-commit.yml in a synchronized repository.
# Install Node.js 24.2 or later and pre-commit locally too. Hook revs must pin release
# commits containing dist/cli.js and a dependency-free package.json.
name: Pre-commit

on:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: pre-commit-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # Runs the pull request's hooks, which are the pull request's own code. A
  # step can change the later steps of its job (through GITHUB_ENV and
  # GITHUB_PATH), so this job can only read and no step of it holds a write
  # token; its fix reaches the next job only as data that job checks.
  hooks:
    name: pre-commit hooks
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      changed: ${{ steps.fixes.outputs.changed }}

          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false

          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

        run: npm install --global --ignore-scripts npm@11.21.2

          # directory, so no module of the checkout can stand in for venv or pip.

          REQUIREMENTS
              echo '::error::Could not install pre-commit 4.7.0 from its pinned hashes; use Python 3.11 to 3.14 on Linux or macOS (x86-64 or arm64) with access to PyPI, or provide pre-commit on PATH.'

            ln -s "$environment/bin/pre-commit" "$environment/commands/pre-commit"

          # A formatter exits 1 when it edits a file. The final pass below
          # decides whether the configuration is now clean.
          pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=never | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/pre-commit.log" || true
      - name: Commit fixes or show the fork patch
        id: fixes
        env:
          SAME_REPOSITORY: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git -c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null add --update
          if ! git diff --cached --quiet; then
            if [[ "$SAME_REPOSITORY" != true ]]; then
              echo 'Apply this patch to the pull request branch, then push again:'
              git diff --cached --binary
              exit 1
            fi
            # Use pre-commit's Python, which already has its YAML dependency.
            # Limit untrusted output to configured ids before creating trailers.
            read -r interpreter < "$(command -v pre-commit)" || interpreter=''
            read -ra python_command <<< "${interpreter#\#!}"
            if [[ "${python_command[0]##*/}" != python* ]]; then
              python_command=(python3)
            fi
            # Isolated (-I): the checkout is not on its module path.
            "${python_command[@]}" -I - <<'PY' || printf 'Apply pre-commit fixes\n' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/pre-commit-message"

          import re
          from pathlib import Path
          import yaml
          config = yaml.safe_load(Path('.pre-commit-config.yaml').read_text())
          configured = {hook['id'] for repo in config['repos'] for hook in repo['hooks']}
          temporary = Path(os.environ['RUNNER_TEMP'])
          hooks = set()
          hook = None
          for line in (temporary / 'pre-commit.log').read_text().splitlines():
              match = re.fullmatch(r'- hook id: (.+)', line)
              if match:
                  hook = match[1] if match[1] in configured else None
              if line == '- files were modified by this hook' and hook:
                  hooks.add(hook)
          (temporary / 'pre-commit-message').write_text('Apply pre-commit fixes\n\n' + ''.join(f'Pre-commit-fix: {hook}\n' for hook in sorted(hooks)))

            git -c user.name='github-actions[bot]' \
                -c user.email='41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com' \
                -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit -F "$RUNNER_TEMP/pre-commit-message"

            mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/pre-commit-fix"

          git diff --exit-code
          git diff --cached --exit-code
      - name: Keep the fix for the publish job

          if-no-files-found: error
          overwrite: true # A re-run of all jobs uploads it again.
          retention-days: 1

  # Pushes the hooks' fix to a same-repository branch and starts genuine CI
  # on that head. The only job with a write token: it starts on a fresh runner,
  # never runs the pull request's code (no hooks, no repository scripts or
  # git hooks) and applies the fix only after checking it as data.

    name: pre-commit fixes
    needs: hooks
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.hooks.result == 'success' && needs.hooks.outputs.changed == 'true' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write # Push the fixing commit to the pull request branch.
      actions: write # Start this workflow and the other CI on the fixing commit.
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: pre-commit-fix
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/pre-commit-fix
      - name: Apply the checked fix
        id: fixes
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # The fix comes from the job that ran the pull request's code: it may
          # change only files the pull request already tracks as regular files,
          # and the commit message keeps only hook ids from its message.
          git_safe() { git -c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null "$@"; }
          refuse() { echo "::error::The pre-commit fix is refused: $1."; exit 1; }
          fix="$RUNNER_TEMP/pre-commit-fix"
          for file in "$fix/fix.patch" "$fix/message"; do
            [[ -f "$file" && ! -L "$file" ]] || refuse 'its files are missing'
          done
          [[ -z "$(git_safe apply --summary -- "$fix/fix.patch")" ]] || refuse 'it creates, deletes, renames or changes the mode of a file'
          while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
            path=${entry#*$'\t'}
            path=${path#*$'\t'}
            mode=''
            read -r -d '' mode _ < <(git_safe ls-files --stage -z -- ":(literal)$path") || true
            [[ "$mode" == 100644 || "$mode" == 100755 ]] || refuse 'it changes a path that is not a tracked regular file'
          done < <(git_safe apply --numstat -z -- "$fix/fix.patch")
          mapfile -t lines < "$fix/message"
          [[ "${lines[0]-}" == 'Apply pre-commit fixes' ]] || refuse 'its message is not the one the hooks job writes'
          message='Apply pre-commit fixes'
          trailers=''
          for line in "${lines[@]:1}"; do
            if [[ "$line" =~ ^Pre-commit-fix:\ [[:graph:]]{1,200}$ ]]; then
              trailers+=$'\n'"$line"
            elif [[ -n "$line" ]]; then
              echo '::warning::A line of the fix message that names no hook id is left out of the fixing commit.'
            fi
          done
          [[ -z "$trailers" ]] || message+=$'\n'"$trailers"
          # Quietly: a warning would echo the patch's text into the log.
          git_safe apply --index --whitespace=nowarn -- "$fix/fix.patch"
          # What was staged decides, since a patch's headers need not state every change.
          [[ -z "$(git_safe diff --cached --no-renames --summary)" ]] || refuse 'it creates, deletes or changes the mode of a file'
          git_safe -c user.name='github-actions[bot]' \
              -c user.email='41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com' \
              commit --no-verify -m "$message"
          echo "sha=$(git_safe rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          HEAD_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref || github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          # No repository-configured subprocess hooks while credentials exist.
          authorization=$(printf 'x-access-token:%s' "$GH_TOKEN" | base64 -w0)
          git -c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c credential.helper= \
              -c "http.https://github.com/.extraheader=AUTHORIZATION: basic $authorization" \
              push origin "HEAD:refs/heads/$HEAD_BRANCH"
      - name: Start genuine CI on the fixing commit
        # A GITHUB_TOKEN push starts no workflows. Dispatch this workflow
        # again and the configured CI so every result belongs to a real job
        # on the fixed head. Synthetic check runs are not proof of CI.
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
          HEAD_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref || github.ref_name }}
          WORKFLOWS: ${{ vars.MDBISYNC_CI_WORKFLOWS }}
          WORKFLOW_REF: ${{ github.workflow_ref }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          own_workflow=${WORKFLOW_REF#*/.github/workflows/}
          own_workflow=${own_workflow%%@*}
          WORKFLOWS="$own_workflow $WORKFLOWS"
          read -ra workflows <<< "$(printf '%s' "$WORKFLOWS" | tr ',\r\n' '   ')"
          for workflow in "${workflows[@]}"; do
            if [[ ! "$workflow" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\.ya?ml$ ]]; then
              echo '::error::MDBISYNC_CI_WORKFLOWS must list workflow file names, such as tests.yml, separated by spaces or commas.'
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          payload=$(node -e 'console.log(JSON.stringify({ref: process.env.HEAD_BRANCH}))')
          for workflow in "${workflows[@]}"; do
            curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \
              -H "Authorization: Bearer $GH_TOKEN" -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
              "https://api.github.com/repos/$REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/$workflow/dispatches" --data "$payload"
          done

  # The check to require: it passes only when the hooks passed and their fix,
  # if any, was published, as when both ran in one job.
  pre-commit:
    needs: [hooks, publish]
    if: ${{ always() }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions: {}
    steps:
      - name: Require the hooks and the published fix
        env:
          HOOKS_RESULT: ${{ needs.hooks.result }}
          PUBLISH_RESULT: ${{ needs.publish.result }}
        run: |
          echo "Hooks: $HOOKS_RESULT. Fix published: $PUBLISH_RESULT."
          [[ "$HOOKS_RESULT" == success && ( "$PUBLISH_RESULT" == success || "$PUBLISH_RESULT" == skipped ) ]]
